properties.content: Question: rat lungworm disease in dogs Answer: Rat lungworm disease, caused by the parasite Angiostrongylus cantonensis, is a serious concern for dogs, particularly in areas with snails and slugs, according to The Times of India. Dogs can contract the disease by ingesting infected snails, slugs, or even contaminated food or water. The parasite can migrate to the brain and spinal cord, leading to severe neurological issues. How Dogs Get Infected:: - Snails and slugs: Rats are the primary host, and their feces contain larvae. Snails and slugs ingest these larvae, becoming intermediate hosts. Dogs then ingest the infected snails or slugs. - Contaminated food/water: Dogs can also get infected by eating food or drinking water contaminated with the larvae or the slime of infected snails/slugs, says The Times of India. Symptoms in Dogs:: - Neurological signs, such as paralysis (especially in the hind legs), abnormal pain responses, and urinary incontinence are common. - Other symptoms can include circling, seizures, and changes in behavior. - In some cases, dogs may not show any symptoms at all, or the symptoms may be mild and non-specific according to the CDC. What to Do:: - Seek veterinary care immediately: If you suspect your dog has rat lungworm disease, take them to a veterinarian as soon as possible. Early treatment is crucial for a positive outcome. - Treatment: Treatment may involve deworming medication and anti-inflammatory drugs, according to PetMD. In severe cases, surgery might be needed to address complications like pneumothorax (air in the chest cavity).
